findings.evidence: template/scripts/publication_queue.py:608-611 computes `resolved_handoff = ... _admission_handoff(root, branch, expected_head)` before `_events`/`_admission`. Previously `_admission_handoff` ran only inside the `if current.get("task_identity") is None or current.get("head") != expected_head` branch (diff lines 712-713 versus 657-658). A retry or re-admission for an already-recorded managed head from a checkout that is not at that head, or without managed state, now raises `managed candidate ... lacks valid exact task-content provenance` or a merge-base error, even though no new record would be written. The same applies to a quick task whose head or origin/main is not present locally, because `_touches_openspec_change` raises on merge-base or diff failure. The spec scenarios only cover the first admission, so this is either an unspecified behavior change or a missing scenario.
findings.summary: admit() now resolves the managed-provenance handoff on every call, before it checks whether the candidate is already admitted or already recorded at the head. The delta contract and design D4 say nothing about this change in idempotent re-admission behavior.
